turns.user: Tin AI hôm nay có gì nổi bật?
turns.assistant_text:
Dưới đây là một số tin tức và thảo luận nổi bật về AI hôm nay:

1. **Rủi ro từ các tư vấn y tế của AI dù có độ chính xác cao**
   - Hơn 300 triệu người hiện dùng ChatGPT để hỏi đáp về sức khỏe mỗi tuần. Tuy nhiên, các chuyên gia cảnh báo rằng ngay cả những câu trả lời chính xác về mặt kỹ thuật vẫn có thể định hướng sai hành vi người bệnh do cách nhấn mạnh hoặc lược bỏ thông tin, đòi hỏi cần có các tiêu chuẩn đánh giá hành vi thay vì chỉ kiểm tra tính chính xác thuần túy.
   - [Chi tiết trên STAT News](https://www.statnews.com/2026/11/10/ai-health-advice-accuracy-messaging-risk-behavioral-benchmarking)

2. **AI khiến việc phát hiện các cuộc gọi khẩn cấp giả mạo trở nên khó khăn hơn**
   - Công nghệ tạo giọng nói và nội dung bằng AI đang bị lợi dụng để thực hiện các cuộc gọi báo án giả (swatting) rất chân thực tới lực lượng cảnh sát, gây khó khăn lớn cho việc xác minh tính xác thực của các tình huống khẩn cấp.
   - [Chi tiết trên NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/nx-s1-5971477/ai-is-making-it-harder-to-detect-fake-emergency-calls)

3. **Vị thế thống trị của Nvidia và thách thức hoàn vốn trong ngành AI**
   - Giới đầu tư tiếp tục bày tỏ lo ngại về mức độ hoàn vốn của các khoản đầu tư khổng lồ vào hạ tầng AI, trong bối cảnh các đối thủ như Google hay AMD vẫn nỗ lực cạnh tranh nhưng chưa thể thay thế sự áp đảo của chip Nvidia trên thị trường.
   - [Chi tiết trên The Conversation](https://theconversation.com/why-is-nvidia-so-powerful-in-the-ai-world-and-what-could-jensen-huangs-scandal-really-cost-296257)

items.summary:
One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] # Someone drained my bank account. Then the real nightmare began | Opinion

## Over time, AI is going to turn our brains to mush. People won't be able to remember phone numbers, basic grammar or directions to places they've visited once or twice without consulting AI overlords.

Portrait of Blake Fontenay

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." [...] People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives.

items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
